items.q: The confirmatory test for PHA is the saline infusion test, performed as:
opts: Infuse 2 litres of normal saline over 4 hours
Give oral salt load for 3 days
items.exp: Saline infusion test: infuse 2 litres NS over 4 hr to expand intravascular volume. (Book p843)

items.q: ‘In PHA the post-saline aldosterone remains unsuppressed (>10 ng/dL); a normal response is a fall in aldosterone.’
items.exp: Volume expansion suppresses aldosterone normally (−); in PHA it stays >10 ng/dL (+). (Book p843)

items.q: After a positive screen, 2 L saline is infused over 4 h and the repeat PAC is 14 ng/dL. The next best step is:
opts: CT abdomen (IOC) to look for B/L hyperplasia vs U/L adenoma
Adrenal vein sampling before any imaging
items.exp: Repeat PAC ≥10 ng/dl confirms PHA; CT abdomen (IOC) then distinguishes B/L hyperplasia from U/L adenoma in the adrenal gland. (Book p843)

items.q: The imaging of choice to localise the adrenal lesion in confirmed PHA is:
items.exp: CT abdomen is the IOC, showing either B/L hyperplasia or U/L adenoma. (Book p843)

items.q: On the confirmatory saline test, a post-infusion PAC above what value supports PHA?
items.exp: Aldosterone >10 ng/dL after saline (unsuppressed) is positive for PHA. (Book p843)
